claims.title: getEbayAppToken / EBAY_SCOPE_INSIGHTS imported from unseen module — verify token failure handling
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**getEbayAppToken / EBAY_SCOPE_INSIGHTS imported from unseen module — verify token failure handling**

`searchEbayInsights` relies on `getEbayAppToken` returning falsy to short-circuit gracefully when the scope isn't approved. This module (`./ebay-oauth`) isn't part of this diff, so its behavior (throwing vs. returning null/undefined on auth failure) can't be verified here. If `getEbayAppToken` throws instead of resolving to a falsy value on a 403/scope-denied response, the `try` block below wouldn't catch it since the call is outside the `try`, causing an unhandled promise rejection instead of the intended graceful `[]` degradation described in the PR.

claims.title: EbayAdapter.searchSoldComps discards soldAt=null items silently and hardcodes condition
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**EbayAdapter.searchSoldComps discards soldAt=null items silently and hardcodes condition**

The mapping sets `condition: 'Not specified'` unconditionally, even though `SoldListing` from `ebay-insights.ts` never actually carries condition data (it's not in the `InsightsItemSale` interface either). This isn't a bug introduced here per se, but it means `PlatformComp.condition` will always report 'Not specified' for eBay comps — worth flagging if downstream logic filters/weights by condition.

claims.title: soldAt can be an empty string but is treated as truthy Date input
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**soldAt can be an empty string but is treated as truthy Date input**

In `EbayAdapter.searchSoldComps`, `r.soldAt` from `searchEbayInsights` is filtered to be non-empty upstream (`.filter((it) => ... it.soldAt && ...)`), so this specific call site is fine. However, `SoldListing.soldAt` is typed as `string` (not `string | null`) yet the filtering guaranteeing non-empty values lives in a separate function far from the type definition — nothing in the type itself prevents a future caller of `searchEbayInsights` internals (e.g. if the filter is ever weakened) from producing an empty `soldAt` string, which would silently construct `new Date('')` → `Invalid Date` here rather than being caught at the type level.

claims.title: priceCents truncated via Math.round without currency/locale validation
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**priceCents truncated via Math.round without currency/locale validation**

`parseFloat(it.price?.value)` assumes the price value is always in the correct currency and decimal format; if eBay ever returns a non-USD marketplace price (unlikely given the hardcoded `EBAY_US` marketplace header, but worth noting) this would silently produce an incorrect priceCents without any currency validation against `it.price?.currency` (not read here).

claims.title: priceCents=0 filtered out even for legitimately free/near-zero-value sales
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**priceCents=0 filtered out even for legitimately free/near-zero-value sales**

The filter `it.priceCents > 0` combined with `Math.round(price*100)` means any parse failure of `it.price?.value` (NaN -> 0) is silently dropped along with genuinely free items. This is consistent with prior SerpAPI behavior, so not a regression, but worth noting there's no distinction/logging between "parse failed" and "filtered as invalid".

claims.title: condition field hardcoded, dropping condition data from API response
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**condition field hardcoded, dropping condition data from API response**

The eBay Marketplace Insights `item_sales/search` response likely includes a `condition` field similar to other eBay APIs, but `searchSoldComps` hardcodes `condition: 'Not specified'` instead of passing through any condition info from `SoldListing`. Since `SoldListing` in ebay-insights.ts doesn't capture a condition field at all, this may be an intentional simplification, but it means condition-based comp filtering downstream (if any) will lose eBay condition data entirely for sold comps.
